As wildfires raged in 2018 forcing his friends, family and neighbours to choose to evacuate or remain to protect the land that defines them filmmaker Josias Tschanz knew he wanted to give his remote community in northern B.C. a voice. Tschanz is bringing his feature length award-winning documentary that he hopes will spark discussion, The Fire In Our Hearts, to Williams Lake on Saturday, Nov. 7 and Thursday, Nov. 12. The film follows communities located directly south of Francois Lake and tells the story of ordinary residents, First Nations and firefighters who chose flight over flight.. “At first it was not a film,” Tschanz said noting, he immigrated to Canada when he was 16 years old from Switzerland and his parents live in the area. At the time of the fires that resulted in ferry access being restricted, Tschanz was smuggled through the toxic smoke on a shipping boat with a friend. “It was just to document things and then create a GoFundMe page, and we had a video that would help people that had lost a lot in the community, but then what happened was the beautiful story of the community coming together and forming an organization.” That organization, Tschanz, said is the Chinook Emergency Response Society which is now a national blueprint on how smaller communities can be part of the solution when there is wildfire and they are too remote to access and provide resources and time. This is where the story takes off, according to Tschanz, telling more than just the fires themselves but the aftermath and what happened during that time. article.title: [americanagnetwork.com] USDA moves nearly $4 million to expand Kansas meat processing
article.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The U.S. Department of Agriculture is moving forward with nearly $4 million in grants to 10 Kansas meat processors to expand capacity and give livestock producers more local processing options. The funding is part of a $57.4 million round covering 147 awards in 40 states through the Meat and Poultry Processing Expansion Program. USDA said it can begin obligating the grants after completing the congressional notification period. The largest Kansas grant, $2 million for Plainview Beef Company in Peabody, will help renovate and equip a processing facility, including cold storage, packaging, rendering and wastewater systems. USDA says the projects aim to expand market access for independent producers and increase competition among processors. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said, “A strong, independent processing sector is essential to our food security, and these Kansas processors build the resilient supply chain this country needs”.

Capacity targets: Kansas grants are projected to raise Hat Creek Butchery’s daily harvest capacity by 200%, Walnut Valley Packing’s processing capacity by about 140%, Randel’s annual capacity by about 67% and T & W Meat’s annual capacity by about 25% (americanagnetwork.com, beefmagazine.com). Other states: The round includes $2.17 million for two Iowa facilities, about $1.1 million for six Illinois projects and $1.07 million for four Wisconsin processors (meatingplace.com). Nebraska award: Wahoo Locker in Nebraska will receive $250,000 for automated packaging equipment for pork and beef products (klkntv.com, meatingplace.com). Program scale: USDA says it has awarded more than $200 million to independent processors through the program since it began (meatingplace.com, americanagnetwork.com).

article.title: [scotsman.com] European researchers test farm water systems as climate swings threaten crops
article.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Scotland’s summer of 2026 brought earlier harvests, heat stress in spring-sown crops and rapidly falling water levels, while research indicates extreme day-to-night temperature swings have become more frequent since the 1980s. Those swings can disrupt crop growth. The Scotsman reported Scottish cereal yields below historic averages, with results varying by crop, soil and location. A Swedish research project is testing a retention-irrigation system that stores water during dry periods and releases it during floods to develop recommendations for its use. In Spain, agricultural cooperatives say farmers are working to adapt and cut emissions but warn that putting innovations into practice depends on farm profitability and adequate funding under the next EU farm-policy reform.

Researchers also observed improvements in blood pressure and nutrient intake, raising questions about longstanding recommendations to choose low-fat dairy.

article.title: [e360.yale.edu] Super El Niño drought threatens crops and deepens global food insecurity
article.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

A powerful El Niño is worsening drought in several food-producing regions. The United Nations World Food Programme warns that it could push 49 million more people into acute food insecurity by the end of 2027, bringing the total to 274 million. Drought has already cut rainfall in northern Sudan to less than half of normal, while dry conditions are affecting crops, livestock and transport in parts of Central America and Southeast Asia. The Famine Early Warning Systems Network projects that 2026-27 production of maize, wheat and rice will be 2.7% below the previous year but still the second-largest on record. El Niño is forecast to peak in December and persist into early 2027. In the Philippines, forecasters expect below-normal rainfall in November and drought conditions in several provinces.

The Famine Early Warning Systems Network projects that 2026-27 production of maize, wheat and rice will be 2.7% below the previous year but still the second-largest on record (yale.edu). El Niño is forecast to peak in December and persist into early 2027. In the Philippines, forecasters expect below-normal rainfall in November and drought conditions in several provinces (leparisien.fr, manilatimes.net). Coastal flooding: California communities from Long Beach to Pacifica are reinforcing beaches and structures, distributing sandbags and preparing for king tides and coastal flooding this winter (npr.org). Storm damage: East Asian storms have closed airports, cut power to 15,000 homes in Okinawa and damaged crops and infrastructure. The region’s accumulated cyclone energy is forecast to reach nearly twice its 30-year average (bbc.co.uk). Fishery disruption: Peru’s anchovy fishery closed early, while global fishmeal output by September was about half its year-earlier level, raising costs for livestock and aquaculture feed (yale.edu). Philippine temperatures: Philippine forecasting agency Pagasa expects warmer-than-average mean air temperatures across most of the country in November (manilatimes.net).

article.title: [Adafruit Blog] Set Up n8n on the Raspberry Pi
article.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

PiMyLifeUp shares how to self-host n8n on your Raspberry Pi. n8n is a self-hosted workflow automation tool. You build each workflow by connecting nodes on a canvas, where each node fetches some data, changes it, or sends it somewhere else. With hundreds of built-in integrations, it is often compared to services like Zapier and Make.

article.title: [ScienceDaily] Astronauts just gave the International Space Station a powerful upgrade
article.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Two astronauts completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station, bringing NASA one step closer to a major power upgrade. Once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30% more available power, supporting critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.
